item.title: Nvidia’s Board Is Meeting to Discuss Jensen Huang’s Future
item.description: Mr. Huang has been under scrutiny for an affair with a woman said to be a Chinese spy, as well as a relationship with an executive at his A.I. chip company.
item.dc:creator: Tripp Mickle and Maggie Haberman
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Few Silicon Valley executives have been as synonymous with their companies as Jensen Huang, the co-founder and chief executive of Nvidia.

item.title: Jensen Huang Said to Have Had Relationship With Nvidia Executive Who Reports to Him
item.description: Mr. Huang, Nvidia’s chief executive, is already facing scrutiny over an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence determined was a Chinese spy.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Mac, Tripp Mickle and Georgia Gee
item.media:credit: Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times
item.media:description: Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, at the company’s annual conference in San Jose, Calif., in March.

item.title: Nvidia’s Stock Price Plummets as Board Is Said to Consider Jensen Huang, CEO’s, Future
item.description: News of the board’s deliberations about Jensen Huang’s job drove Nvidia’s stock down more than 8 percent in after-hours trading.
item.dc:creator: Michael Corkery and Jason Karaian

item.title: Scott Colom Will Be Mississippi’s Third Black Senator. Who Were the First Two?
item.description: Mr. Revels took his seat two days after Mississippi was readmitted to the union after the Civil War. Mr. Bruce served just before white leaders ushered in the Jim Crow era.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: Brady-Handy Collection, via Library of Congress
item.media:description: Hiram Revels became the first Black man to serve in the U.S. Senate after being elected by the Mississippi state legislature in 1870.

item.title: A Diminished Justice Dept. Braces for Fresh Fights After Midterm Loss
item.description: The upheaval points to a broader dilemma spurred by the election: whether the department can carry out President Trump’s priorities as career officials eye the exits and senior department officials resign.
item.dc:creator: Glenn Thrush and Alan Feuer
item.media:credit: Nathan Howard for The New York Times
item.media:description: Attorney General Todd Blanche has made clear that he intends to use the Justice Department to fight off any attempts by Congress to investigate the administration.

item.title: Democrats Face Backlash After Missing Hegseth Impeachment Vote
item.description: Eleven Democrats were absent, helping Republicans shelve the charges against the defense secretary. It drew sharp criticism a week after the party’s sweeping election victories.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison
item.media:description: Democratic absences during the vote raised questions about party leaders’ hold on their caucus at a critical time.

item.title: Strike on Gaza Hospital Kills at Least 6 and Injures 20, Rescuers Say
item.description: Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis was attacked despite the 2025 cease-fire. A surgeon, an official and a disabled patient were among the victims, a witness said.
